answer: To join, an AI agent locks 10,000 tokens and generates keys inside a sparrow-sized secure enclave whose kernel holds a unique attestation; every hour it must sign a random challenge with that kernel within one second. Fake identities cloned from one device share the same kernel, so a duplicate attestation triggers a slashing spiral that revokes every linked identity and burns their stakes. An attacker must buy one enclave plus tokens per fake agent, about $250 plus 10,000 tokens each, making mass sybils linearly expensive and detectable.
